answer: No. Git remote sync for a managed space is primarily a backup mechanism (and for history) and "should not be considered for any type of collaboration"; for collaboration, use a shared Server space instead.

## Is the Git remote sync for a managed space meant for working together with other people?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/Git Sync.md] ---
### Syncing with a remote

# Syncing with a remote
A managed space can automatically fetch, merge, and push its Git repository. This is primarily a **backup mechanism**, it should not be considered for any type of collaboration.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Revisions.md] ---
### Syncing with a remote

# Syncing with a remote
A managed space can fetch, merge and push its revision repository. Follow [[Guide/Git Sync]] for setup, timing and recovery. This is primarily for history and backup. Use a shared Server space for collaboration.

### Untitled

Git is a [free and open source version control system](https://git-scm.com/) originally developed by Linus Torvalds (of Linux fame) and the de-facto standard in the industry.

SilverBullet uses Git for [[Revisions]]. Managed spaces can optionally fetch, merge and push to a remote through [[Guide/Git Sync]]. For access from another device, compare the alternatives in [[Guide/Devices and Publishing]].
